desc:
You are given an array nums of positive integers. You may apply any number of operations, each on any element:

  • if the element is even, divide it by 2;
  • if the element is odd, multiply it by 2.

The deviation of the array is the difference between its largest and its smallest element. Return the minimum deviation that can be reached.

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]  result = 1
double 1 -> [2, 2, 3, 4], halve 4 -> [2, 2, 3, 2]   max 3, min 2

nums = [4, 1, 5, 20, 3]  result = 3
hints: Each element can only take values from a short chain. Write down which values an odd element and an even element can reach.
An odd x can become x or 2x. An even x can become any of x, x/2, x/4, ... down to its odd part. So you can first double every odd element and then only ever need to decrease elements.

After doubling the odds, everything can only be halved (while even). Repeatedly halve the maximum with a max-heap, tracking the current minimum and the best max - min seen; stop when the maximum is odd.
editorial: Normalise: double every odd number. Now every element is even-or-odd-but-already-maximal, and the set of values an element can take is its current value divided by 2 repeatedly, down to its odd part. The doubled value is the largest in each chain, so the starting state has every element at its maximum.

From there the only useful move is to lower the current maximum, because lowering anything else cannot reduce the max. Keep a max-heap and the minimum mn of the current values. Compute max - mn as a candidate, then if the maximum is even, halve it, update mn and repeat; if the maximum is odd it cannot be reduced and no later state can be better, so stop.
Every element is halved at most about 21 times, so there are at most about 100,000 heap steps: O(n log n log M) time (M is the largest value), O(n) memory. The result is the minimum candidate seen.
